steps.say: This lesson shows the project's own **gadgets** and what each one is for. A gadget is a small app that lives in a Prism panel: a page you look at, and sometimes a part that runs commands for it in the background.
They are listed here. This project has four of its own: kernel tests, feature tests, the VM's serial log, and performance fixes.
**Kernel test results** runs `make test` and shows what passed. Its **Run tests** button starts a real build and two boots in QEMU, so press it only when you mean to.
Its checks are lines the boot must print, grouped into milestones: kernel core, cores and scheduling, user space. They mirror the list in tests/boot_test.sh.
This is what the button runs, inside WSL. It keeps a history of runs, so you can compare today's boot with yesterday's.
**Feature test runs** watches the end-to-end suite: the launcher, windows, apps, the companion, the tray, Settings, the terminal and more, each in a VM of its own. A whole run takes about an hour.
**Run all** starts scripts/feature_checks.py. The gadget reads build/feature-checks/events.jsonl as that script writes it, so it also follows a run started by hand.

**The OS VM serial log** follows the log of the VM that Operating System.cmd starts. A serial log is the text the kernel and programs print while the system runs. The gadget sorts its lines into AI calls, errors, timeouts and screens.
Be careful with **Restart the OS**: it stops every running qemu-system-x86_64, test VMs included, then starts Operating System.cmd again.
**Performance fixes** lists the slow spots found so far, the plan for each, and the numbers before and after each fix.
Each measurement is one of the project's own test scripts, tests/*_win.py. Each one boots a VM, so only one runs at a time.
Prism also brings gadgets of its own. **System pulse** shows how busy this PC is. That is worth a look before you start a test VM, since vmkit gives each one 12 GB of memory by default.
Prism's other built-in gadgets include **Graphics card** (gpu), **Decisions** and **Profiling**. They are listed in the same panel.

The agent can use these gadgets too: each one gives it tools, such as `kernel_test_latest`, `tests_status` or `serial_summary`. That is the end of the series. Lesson 01 is the place to start again, and the gadgets are where to look after every change.
